dated_bounds.note: AN APPEARANCE IN THE TOWN'S PRINT, AND NOTHING FURTHER. The Chicago Democrat of 1835-06-24 names 'Mr. Secrelary FIELD' in the claim read as chicago_democrat_1835_06_24#c004, so the reading dates an appearance of this person in the town's press and `here_by` is null: a name in print is not a body in the town, and a notice can be signed elsewhere and reprinted here. Under the evidence ladder ratified 2026-09-03 a source EARLIER than the scene date corroborates and dates and never promotes, and a source LATER than it does not promote either. THE IDENTITY IS INFERRED AND THE PAGE IS NOT: the issue is deposited, dated and numbered in data/research/newspapers/corpus.json, and what no source states is that the name the paper prints is the person on this card — the register joins them under its own written note. No grade moves here and the identity is neither reopened nor hardened.

persons.note: A CONTEMPORARY CHICAGO PAPER OF 1833-1835 PRINTS THIS PERSON BY NAME IN THE TOWN. Read from newspaper_1833_1835. THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G1b), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: everything except the person and the sources — no dwelling, no trade, no origin, no family, no party. A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. newspaper_1833_1835 names this person at Chicago by 24 June 1835 and nothing says when they came. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the person was at Chicago by 1 July 1835 on this record's own evidence. No figure is drawn (L1). THE SECOND PRESBYTERIAN ROLL — A NAME ON A CHURCH LIST THAT OPENS IN 1842, AND NEVER AN 1835 FACT. The 1892 printed membership roll of the Second Presbyterian Church of Chicago, read line by line into this repository, carries 1 line whose surname and given initial agree with this person's — “Field, Mrs. Sarah | Letter. | August 6, 1842. | Dismissed.” (second_presb_0542, printed page 186), admitted 1842-08-06 by letter. Under the rule that decided it: Surname 'Field' folds to the same string as the roll line's, and the given name of both begins S. WHAT THE MATCH MINTS OR REGRADES: “NOTHING. A line on a roll that opens in June 1842 cannot place a person in the town of July 1835, and this file makes no proposal that it does. What a match IS: the same surname and initial, in Chicago, within seven years — a lead for a later pass that is allowed to write people.” THE LINE IS A MARRIED WOMAN'S ENTRY, and the crosswalk's own Mrs rule governs what it can have met: “a line flagged a_married_womans_entry that meets a MAN in the 1835 layer has met his name, not him: it corroborates that the name was a Chicago name in the 1840s and it does not put that man on this roll.” The match is filed rather than suppressed, because a suppressed match is invisible and a flagged one can be argued with. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE: under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the roll is handed to the card as a thing a reader may weigh, and the verdict stays with T-0515, which applies the ladder against every source at once.

roles.note: PRINTED AGAINST THIS NAME IN THE 1833-1835 PRESS and carried here from the newspaper gazetteer (T-1254, by tools/derive_resident_roles.py). The gazetteer holds its trades on the PERSON record and not on a single issue, so the bound is the run of this person's own dated mentions, 1835-06-24 to 1835-06-24, and the grade is `inferred`: the paper printed the trade, and the resident programme's identity rule tied the printing to this card. The scene date falls outside that run, so this role does not stand in the 1835 view.

age_band.note: AN AGE BAND, NEVER A YEAR. No source this project holds bears on when this person was born, so the band is drawn from the only committed sex by age distribution the project has - the 1840 Chicago schedule, five years after the scene and a town twice the size - seeded by this person's own id ('field_secretary:age_bands_1840'). AND THE CONDITIONING IS THE MODEL'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: that a roll naming a person in their own right names somebody 15 or over. The 1840 schedule counts a child as a tally inside a household and never as a correspondent; 15 rather than 20 because an apprentice or a journeyman stands on a trade roll. No source states this rule. No exact year is written, because a year drawn from a decadal band would read as a record of a birth.
